   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-44 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-44 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-44 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 21, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  2
   Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2022

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2021-22 Adopted Investment Policy
  (Resolution No. 21-30 dated July 20, 2021) and California Government Code
  Section 53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The June 2022
  Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with
  the City’s adopted 2021-22 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for June 2022.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 22-49 RESCINDING RESOLUTION NO. 21-12 AND
  ADOPTING RULES OF ORDER FOR THE CONDUCT OF CITY MEETINGS IN
  ORDER TO UPDATE THE MEETING SCHEDULE, AND STANDARDIZE
  ATTENDANCE, DISCLOSURE, AND REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS

  From time to time, revisions are required to the Rules of Order governing City
  meetings in order to conform with changes the City Council or Commissions
  have requested, and as efficiencies are identified to facilitate the orderly
  conduct of meetings. Resolution No. 22-49 would rescind the current Rules of
  Order and establish updated Rules of Order for City meetings incorporating a
  new meeting schedule for the Community Services Commission and
  standardized attendance, disclosure and regulatory requirements.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-49 rescinding
  Resolution No. 21-12 and adopting revised Rules of Order for the conduct of
  City meetings.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 22-45 APPROPRIATING ADDITIONAL FUNDING IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $4,692 FOR THE OMITTED SALES TAX OF $14,145 ON THE
  PREVIOUSLY-AUTHORIZED PURCHASE CONTRACT FOR AN ALTEC LIFT
  BUCKET TRUCK

  On April 19, 2022, City Council approved the purchase of a new Ford F-550
  Truck with an Altec Lift Bucket System via a Sourcewell contract for the Field
  Operations Division. Unfortunately, the sales tax amount was inadvertently
  omitted on the quote and was overlooked by staff. The original proposed quote
  for $142,547 did not include sales tax on the vehicle. Staff has since acquired
  an updated quote that includes our 10.25% sales tax. The new purchase price
  with sales tax included is $156,692. The adopted Fiscal Year 2021-22 Budget
  included $152,000 from the Gas Tax budget account 124-800-41-99-767 for
  the purchase of an aerial lift bucket truck. If approved, an appropriation of
  $4,692 from the Gas Tax fund to budget account 124-800-41-99-767 will be
  required.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-45 and
  authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Altec Industries
  Inc., in an amount not to exceed $156,692, which is inclusive of sales tax from
  the Gas Tax budget account 124-800-41-99-767 and void the previously-
  approved purchase order request for $142,547.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 22-43 APPROVING THE FILING OF A GRANT
  APPLICATION FOR FUNDING FROM THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN SPACE DISTRICT FOR THE VINCENT LUGO
  PARK ACCESS PATH AND BRIDGE REPLACEMENT PROJECT

  In November 2016, the County of Los Angeles voters approved the Safe, Clean
  Neighborhood Park, Open Space, Beaches, River Protection, and Water
  Conservation Measure, also known as Measure A. The Measure A grant is
  funded through an annual special tax on all taxable real property in the County.
  Funding is available for projects that repair and upgrade parks and recreational
  facilities; create new parks; preserve and protect open spaces and beaches, and
  support recreational programming. The Los Angeles County Regional Park and
  Open Space District (RPOSD) is responsible for implementing and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  4
   administering the Measure A grants. RPOSD facilitates online grant application
  and administrative processes and provides oversight. There is no fiscal impact
  on the budget at this time.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 22-43;
  2. Authorize the filing of the Grant Application with the Los Angeles County
  Regional Park and Open Space District; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any further
  documents required for the project's funding.

  H. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 22-01 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $845,000 TO COLICH & SONS, LIMITED PARTNERSHIP FOR THE
  SUBMERSIBLE PUMP INSTALLATION FOR SEWER PUMP STATION
  PROJECT AT THE CITY’S SEWER LIFT STATION

  The City’s Sewer Lift Station is located at the corner of McGroarty Street and
  Mission Road, and was constructed in 2016 as a requirement of the Alameda
  Corridor-East (ACE) Train Trench Project. It is in need of multiple upgrades due
  to design and function deficiencies, which has led to multiple pump failures and
  two sewage overflows. The existing pump design with two Gorman-Rupp 40
  horsepower-motor pumps, is unable to effectively process thick grease and
  solid materials, which frequently enter our pumps and overheats the motors.
  This outdated design is prone to losing prime, fouling and cavitation at the
  impellers, and plugged at inlets, causing the loss of one pump and progressive
  overheating of the other. Public Works Staff has had to respond frequently to
  address these problems during events and weekends, in recent months. Funds
  are available in the Fiscal Year 2022-23 approved budget with Capital
  Improvement Project (CIP) 4-20-01 (Phase 2) and under sewer budget accounts
  122-800-38-97-403.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve plans and specifications for Installation of Three Submersible Pumps
  at the Sewer Lift Station per Construction Contract No. 22-01;

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  5
   2. Award the Contract to Colich & Sons, LP and authorize the City Manager to
  execute Construction Contract No. 22-01 with Colich & Sons, LP for a total bid
  amount of $845,000; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Colich & Sons,
  LP for an amount not to exceed $925,000 which includes a 10% construction
  contingency.

  I. RESOLUTION NO. 22-46 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 400 BLOCK OF SEGOVIA AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Louis Felix, resident at
  453 Segovia Avenue, for a temporary street closure. The purpose of this request
  is to hold a block party which will be held on Sunday, August 14, 2022, on the
  400 block of Segovia Avenue between Roses Road and Leslie Drive from 4:00
  p.m. to 8:00 p.m. There is no fiscal impact to the budget for this event.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-46 authorizing
  closure on Segovia Avenue between Roses Road and Leslie Drive from 4:00 p.m.
  to 8:00 p.m. on Sunday, August 14, 2022.

  J. ACCEPTANCE OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY MEASURE B GRANT FUNDING IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $163,860 FOR THE PURCHASE OF THREE CARDIAC
  MONITOR DEFIBRILLATORS

  The San Gabriel Fire Department has been awarded $163,860 grant, form Los
  Angeles County Measure B funds, a special assessment approved by voters in
  2002 to improve Emergency Medical Services, Trauma Centers and Bioterrorism
  Response capabilities within Los Angeles County. The grant funds will be used
  to purchase three Zoll X Series Cardiac Monitor Defibrillators and upgrade
  current X Series Monitor Defibrillators. The City was awarded $163,860 from the
  County of Los Angeles Measure B Special Assessment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Make a motion to adopt Resolution No. 22-51, which will increase account
  186-3234 by $163,860 (revenue account);
  2. Increase the Fire Department budget by $163,860 in account 124-761-57-
  99-380;

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  6
   3. Authorize the City Manager to accept the Measure B award per the
  attachments of “Measure B Advisory Board Recommendation for Funding”
  and “Los Angeles County Measure B Monitor Purchase Agreement;” and
  4. Authorize the Fire Chief to purchase three (3) Zoll X Series Cardiac Monitors
  and upgrades for existing monitors as specified in attachment “Zoll Medical
  Quotation.”

  K. FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 FIRE DEPARTMENT SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT
  OPEN PURCHASE ORDERS

  The San Gabriel Fire Department, in the course of daily operations, maintains a
  supply of expendable items and durable equipment to fulfill its mission. Open
  purchase orders are requested at the beginning of each Fiscal Year (FY) used to
  keep the Department stocked with personal protective equipment, paramedic
  and firefighting supplies, delivered on an as-needed basis. Vendors, reviewed
  regularly, are selected through competitive bid, piggyback and cooperative
  purchasing agreements. Paramedic and Firefighting equipment and supplies
  are budgeted for FY 2022-2023 as line items.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of open
  purchase orders in the amount of $60,000 to Lift Assist, Incorporated and in the
  amount of $55,000 to Municipal Emergency Services. Pursuant to Title III,
  Section 34.35 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, the City may piggyback on a
  contract or cooperative purchasing agreement prepared by and processed
  through another local, state, or federal government agency.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF POLICE DEPARTMENT LEXIPOL
  POLICY, SECTION 707, MILITARY EQUIPMENT, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY
  BILL (AB) 481 MILITARY EQUIPMENT ACQUISITION, USE, AND
  REPORTING

  In the wake of several high-profile incidents, recent policing reform efforts have
  resulted in changes in legislation that directly impact policing in the City of San
  Gabriel. As a result of emerging concerns related to the use of military-style

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  7
   equipment by local law enforcement, and the requisite oversight and
  accountability, Assembly Bill 481 was passed. It mandates certain requirements
  for the acquisition, use, and funding of military-style equipment including the
  development of “Council”-approved and publically-posted Department policies
  and procedures. This item, if approved, would meet that requirement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and adopt San Gabriel Police
  Department, Lexipol Manual Section 707, Military Equipment, and associated
  protocols pursuant to AB 481.

  B. LOGO AND BRANDING GUIDE FOR RIDESG TRANSIT

  The Community Services Department will provide the City Council options for
  the RideSG logo and branding guide.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the selected logo and color
  palette for the new transit program.

  C. CITY CLERK DEPARTMENT UPDATE

  The City Clerk Department serves as a guardian for transparency and
  accessibility to the public, as well as the historian for legislative actions. This
  presentation will provide an overview of the history, duties, accomplishments,
  and ongoing projects of the Department.

  Recommended Action:

  This is an informational item only; no action required.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 19, 2022  8
   11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The City Council will adjourn the meeting in memory of Esther Woo Jan.

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, August 16, 2022 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
